reviews.quote: No professional review found for this line as of 2026-11; ratings inferred from specs and sibling-line reviews.

praises: Cheapest way into the gram name — light 15.6" chassis well under most rivals' weight
Windows 11 Pro and vPro-class manageability at a small-business price
Numeric keypad plus touch screen suit office and POS-style use
U-series chip runs cool and near-silent on office workloads
Lightweight for a 15.6" with numpad (~1.65 kg est.)
complaints: FHD 16:9 60 Hz panel with ~250 nits is dim and washed out vs any gram Pro display
Ultra 7 255U is a low-power office part — noticeably slower than H-series under multitask load
Plasticky chassis build is a step down from the magnesium-nano-carbon grams
64GB/2TB tier at $3,099 makes no sense next to the gram Pro 16
Speakers and webcam are basic; Wi-Fi 6E only, no Wi-Fi 7

design_philosophy: The gram Book is LG's value sub-line: the gram lightness pitch at office-laptop prices, built on a low-power Arrow Lake-U platform with Win11 Pro for small businesses. It drops the premium chassis materials, high-res panels, and Copilot+ NPU of the mainline grams. This entry consolidates the three RAM/storage tiers, which differ only in memory and price — the entry tier is the one that makes sense.
